summary: Adversary r2 FAIL on plan rev 2 60b693e0 (delta 91c82e89..60b693e0: docs/design/B12-outreach-plan.md + B12-outreach-plan-cells.md). Prior: 12 FIXED (ADV-1, 10-19, 21), 9 PARTIALLY_FIXED (ADV-2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 20). New: 0 BLOCKING, 11 MAJOR, 3 MINOR. Checked against code and true: run.access at runtime.ts:300 runs before journal.reserve at :306, and the app clock is read at :318; seller shared transition lock at commercial-sales.ts:339, CMD050 FOR NO KEY UPDATE at :369 + exclusive at :372, owner at :857, unassignProspects UPDATE at :618 (the plan cites :617, the method head); L3/L4/L8 are advisory xact locks (0001:267-273); units run READ COMMITTED (runtime-transaction.ts:55), so a trigger statement after its lock sees the committed row; effect_now is at 0038:12; the 2026-12-24 case is correct ([2027-01-04T15:00Z, 2027-01-07T15:00Z): Dec 25 and Jan 1 are holidays in both calendars, and both zones are UTC-5 in winter); GAP-SUP-1 is reachable and goes red without the trigger L8 at 0029:991 (without it CMD045's unique check on prospects_one_live_per_organization, 0029:359, waits for CMD064's UPDATE and then inserts a live prospect of the suppressed organization); the current_seller_id census (28 lines, 26 policy lines) is exact; origin/main 99266f52 tops out at KA094 and KC027; KA098 and KC034..KC037 appear in the sqlstate.ts, KC-CODES.md or migrations of no local ref (refs/heads + refs/remotes). The only worktree text naming them is b12/outreach's own plan and plan-b15-b17-b18 67e3e616, which only says 'KA098 is not claimed' (5ef94d6f:docs/design/B15-B17-B18-local-plan.md:131, 0 KA codes). Risk: that plan calls KA098 'the next free code', so the coordinator must reserve KA098 and KC028-037 for B12 on the board before B15 rev 2. D-33: the plan has no agency/company ranking, no segment read and no CRM write; b12-d33 has planted controls; A17 forbids CRM ports. Rejected because L4 (the person cap added in rev 2, taken by almost every writer right after L3) creates a lock-order cycle in D4 and moves the real meeting point of most L3/L9 RACE cells to L4, so red-with-the-lock-removed fails. There are also gaps in the opt-out wire format, suppression idempotency, the draft-state edges and two revocation pairs. Recorded decisions: (1) a post-claim opt-out is not recalled: allowed, because the reference says 'before queued sends are claimed'; (2) a grant/sender/seller authority change after the D2 COMMIT and before the bounded call: allowed, because the reference requires the recheck 'before dispatch' (at the claim) and the external call cannot be atomic with it, on two conditions: the window stays bounded (callBound < lease TTL, with the D2 EXPIRY boundary cell present) and every residual has a cell. The sender-revocation residual has no cell (ADV-28), and the reference's acceptance list names 'sender revocation during dispatch'. The family-coverage table waits for the PASS round (verdict FAIL). The ADV-4 family recurs (ADV-23/24, reachability for the second round): a root-cause template rule is required before round 3.

findings.title: D4 takes L4/L9 through the intent trigger after it already holds L7/L10/L12: a lock-order cycle with CMD063/D2 on the AUTH_REVOKED path, and D4 is missing from the section G writer census
findings.reproduction: D4 trace (plan:143): L3(P) -> L7(S) FOR NO KEY UPDATE (AUTH_REVOKED) -> L10(D) -> L12(I) -> UPDATE intent SUBMITTING->NOT_SENT. That edge leaves COUNTED, so by section G (plan:102-103, 116) and cells:19 the BEFORE UPDATE trigger takes L4(X) and L9(G) at that point, after L7/L10/L12. This contradicts 'No actor takes a lower L after a higher one' (plan:108). At the same time, CMD063 of person X on prospect P2 (plan:130) runs L1 -> L2 -> L3(P2) -> L4(X) excl -> L5 -> L6 -> L7(S) FOR SHARE and waits for D4's FOR NO KEY UPDATE on S, while D4 waits for the L4(X) that CMD063 holds: deadlock (40P01). D2 of another intent of X (plan:135, L4 before L7 shared) forms the same cycle. If D4 is the victim, a definite AUTH_REVOKED turns into SEND_UNCERTAIN via D5 (KC029 then blocks the prospect until a human reconciles), and the sender is not marked REVOKED. Separately, D4 NOT_SENT (AUTH_REVOKED, REJECTED_DEFINITIVE, NOT_ATTEMPTED, plan:20-21) lowers both the grant count and the person cap, yet it is missing from the section G grant row (plan:115) and has no pair cell.
findings.acceptance_criterion: Every actor that moves an intent into or out of COUNTED (CMD063, D2, D4, D5 if it does, CMD064, opt-out, HUMAN observation) takes L4 and L9 in the global order before L5..L12. The trigger only re-enters locks already held, or asserts that they are held. Section G lists D4 as a -1 writer of both aggregates, with a pair cell. The order claim at plan:108 holds for every trace.

findings.title: A late provider answer after a lease takeover cannot close SEND_UNCERTAIN: the old owner's D4 is fenced at L13, so GAP-DI-7's expected outcome cannot happen and A3's claim is false in that case
findings.reproduction: A3 (plan:24) says 'A late provider answer after D5 is evidence: SEND_UNCERTAIN -> PROVIDER_ACCEPTED'. GAP-DI-7 (plan:149) says 'D4 of the old owner and D5 of the new owner held at L3 in both orders: ... the late answer then closes it PROVIDER_ACCEPTED'. A new owner's D5 runs only after claim_lease has moved the fence (plan:144-145). D4 ends with L13 = holdDispatchLease(resource, owner, fence) FOR SHARE (commission-service-access.ts:166-180), which raises LEASE_FENCED for the old fence in either L3 order. So D4 always rolls back, the answer is lost and SEND_UNCERTAIN stays. Only the same-owner case (D5 at submitted_at + callBound while D4 is slow) can close it.
findings.acceptance_criterion: The plan states which late answers can close SEND_UNCERTAIN: same fence only, or a fence-independent evidence path that records the provider ref without a new submission. The cells assert exactly that: a fenced D4 leaves SEND_UNCERTAIN with zero submissions, and a late D4 of the same owner closes it once, with its ref.
findings.failing_test: b12-dispatch-cells :: 'GAP-DI-7 (takeover): the old owner's D4 after the new owner's D5 is LEASE_FENCED, SEND_UNCERTAIN kept, one submission' + 'GAP-DI-7b (same owner): D5 at the bound then the late D4: PROVIDER_ACCEPTED with its ref, one activity'.

findings.title: One-click opt-out wire format: the standard admission refuses an RFC 8058 POST (form-encoded body, no envelope headers); no cell sends the real request; DKIM coverage of the two headers is a live half the plan does not list
findings.reproduction: RFC 8058: List-Unsubscribe carries one HTTPS URI; the receiver POSTs 'List-Unsubscribe=One-Click' as application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart/form-data, with no cookies and no context; the DKIM signature must cover List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post. The api's admission refuses anything that is not JSON (packages/application/src/api/admission.ts:115, CONTENT_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED) and checks the envelope headers first (public-routes.ts:11, the manual 10 order). The plan decides cookie/Origin (D-B12O-13), but not the content type, the body, the envelope headers or the journal key when there is no Idempotency-Key. 'OPT-OUT OK: one-click POST without Origin' does not fix the request shape. A JSON-only handler therefore passes every title while every real Gmail/Yahoo one-click unsubscribe fails (18: 'a working opt-out'; reference: 'Do not require login').
findings.acceptance_criterion: The opt-out POST admits exactly the RFC 8058 request through the real HTTP server (both content types, body List-Unsubscribe=One-Click, no envelope headers, no Idempotency-Key) and refuses other bodies. The payload title asserts exactly one HTTPS URI in List-Unsubscribe. Section 6 lists DKIM coverage of both headers as a live PART (B14/B19) with its verification step.
findings.failing_test: b12-opt-out :: 'OPT-OUT OK (RFC 8058): POST Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded body List-Unsubscribe=One-Click with no other header through the HTTP server suppresses the contact; the multipart/form-data variant too' (red today: 415/CONTENT_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED).

findings.title: A second suppression of an already suppressed key or prospect is undefined: prospect_suppressions is UNIQUE (key_kind, suppression_key) and SUPPRESSED -> SUPPRESSED is not a listed transition, so a complaint after an opt-out (or an opt-out through the follow-up's token) rolls back and the complaint pause never fires
findings.reproduction: 0029:371 has prospect_suppressions_one_per_key UNIQUE (key_kind, suppression_key); 0029:100-106 list X -> SUPPRESSED for every X except SUPPRESSED itself; prospects_transition is at 0029:732. CMD064 SUPPRESSED commits 'activity + suppression row + own prospect SUPPRESSED' in one unit (plan:151-152); the opt-out INSERTs a suppression and sets the prospect SUPPRESSED (plan:159-160). Example: contact K opts out through the first message, then complains (CMD064 SUPPRESSED, reason COMPLAINT). The INSERT violates the unique key (or the prospect UPDATE is refused), the whole unit rolls back, no COMPLAINT activity is stored, and A12's pause (plan:57) never triggers for that seller. The same happens with a second token of the same contact (first message + follow-up) and with an owner ORGANIZATION suppression of a prospect whose contact is already suppressed. KA097(f) 'one SUPPRESSED per (prospect, key)' does not decide this.
findings.acceptance_criterion: Each suppression writer states what it does when the key and/or prospect is already suppressed (activity recorded, existing suppression row kept, prospect not re-transitioned), and the health pause reads the reason on the activity. Cells: complaint after opt-out, second token of one contact, organization after contact.

findings.title: No cell discriminates the outreach calendar rule (union of US federal and Colombian holidays, judged in both zones); the US observed-day rule and its source are unstated
findings.reproduction: A10 (plan:45-48) admits a weekday that is a holiday neither under 5 U.S.C. 6103 nor in COLOMBIA_HOLIDAYS (holidays.ts:142, covering 2026-2030), judged in both America/New_York and America/Bogota. Every cell uses Dec 25 and Jan 1 (holidays in both calendars) or weekends (GAP-SE-18, GAP-SE-20), so an implementation with only one calendar, or only one zone, passes. The plan does not say whether 6103(b) in-lieu days are holidays (2026-07-03 Fri for Jul 4 Sat; 2027-06-18, 2027-07-05, 2027-12-24, 2027-12-31), and it gives no source or version for the US list (17: 'current verified calendar', 'Do not substitute ... an unverified weekday-only approximation').
findings.acceptance_criterion: The rule for the US list (including observed days) and its source are recorded with the seed version. Cells: a Colombian-only holiday (2027-01-11) and a US-only holiday (2027-01-18) each refuse a first contact and do not count as a follow-up business day; a summer instant that is a business day in one zone but not the other (e.g. 2027-07-02T23:30-05:00 Bogota = 2027-07-03T00:30 New York, an observed day) is refused.
findings.failing_test: cmd063 :: 'DENY (calendar union): first contacts on 2027-01-11 and 2027-01-18 refused (KC032 OUTSIDE_BUSINESS_DAY); a follow-up window across 2027-01-18 opens one business day later'.

findings.title: KA098 forged control (a) is vacuous because organization_label is already immutable for every role (prospects_immutable 0029:730-731); the real risk of the new seller/outreach UPDATE policies (owner_seller_id, another seller's prospect) has no control
findings.reproduction: The forbid_column_change trigger at 0029:730-731 already covers prospect_id, organization_label, organization_key, business_contact_id, source_evidence_hash, jurisdiction, registered_by_* and created_at. With KA098 dropped, KA098(a) is still refused, with the old guard's code, so the control stays green and fails rule 12 ('each control red alone with its guard dropped'). The new prospects_seller_suppress / prospects_outreach_suppress policies newly expose owner_seller_id and state (D-B12O-12, plan:206-208). No control covers a seller setting owner_seller_id to itself, or suppressing a prospect that is not assigned to it.
findings.acceptance_criterion: Each KA098 control goes red when only KA098 (or only the new policy's USING clause) is dropped: a non-owner UPDATE of owner_seller_id is refused; a seller UPDATE of a prospect not assigned to it is refused (policy USING); the OK sibling goes through the production writer.
findings.failing_test: b12-outreach-migrations :: 'KA098 (a): forged seller UPDATE owner_seller_id = self refused; KA098 (d): seller suppressing a prospect of another seller refused; OK: CMD064 SUPPRESSED through the writer'.

findings.title: 'Provider warnings: no ingestion source exists in V1' is false: D4 receives Gmail 403/429 refusals (quota, rate, policy), and R2 18 pauses new outreach on any provider warning
findings.reproduction: 18 'Outreach cadence and health' says 'any complaint/provider warning pauses new outreach pending diagnosis'. A3 (plan:20) classifies 403 and 429 answered before acceptance as REJECTED_DEFINITIVE -> NOT_SENT and nothing more; A12 (plan:58) declares provider warnings N/A. A seller who hits Gmail's sending limit or a policy refusal keeps queuing first contacts (each ending NOT_SENT), with no pause and no owner diagnosis.
findings.acceptance_criterion: The plan decides which provider answers are warnings (at least the 403 quota/policy refusals and 429) and pauses the person (KC034) until RecordOutreachDiagnosis, or explains with an R2 citation why a send refusal is not a warning. A DENY cell covers it.
findings.failing_test: b12-dispatch-cells :: 'DENY (provider warning): a Gmail 429 at D3 records NOT_SENT(PROVIDER_REJECTED:429) and a new first contact of that person is 409 KC034 until the diagnosis'.

findings.title: '12 business days > 14 calendar days makes a second [follow-up] unreachable under both' is false under the rolling reading of 'no more than three total messages over fourteen calendar days'
findings.reproduction: With messages at day 0, at day 7 or later (5 business days) and at day 16 or later (12 business days), no 14-day window ever holds more than two, so under that reading the reference does not forbid the second follow-up. Dropping it is a stricter, allowed choice, but the stated reason is wrong (a rule 13 claim).
findings.acceptance_criterion: The sentence records the choice as a conservative decision (sequence window = 14 days from the first message) and drops the false 'under both'.

findings.title: A per-network opt-out rate limit can refuse valid one-click opt-outs, which mail providers send from shared networks
findings.reproduction: The plan says 'the 21st POST in 60 s from one client network is ADMISSION_LIMITED and writes nothing'. RFC 8058 POSTs come from the receiver's infrastructure (one network for all Gmail recipients), so a burst, or an attacker spraying unknown tokens from that network, makes valid opt-outs fail, and the receiver is not required to retry. The reference asks to 'rate-limit abuse', not to refuse a valid opt-out.
findings.acceptance_criterion: The limiter never refuses a valid token: either limit only unknown-token lookups, or answer with a retryable status while the suppression path for valid tokens stays unlimited. Cell: 'the 21st POST in 60 s with a valid token suppresses'.
findings.failing_test: b12-opt-out :: 'OPT-OUT (rate, valid token): after 20 unknown-token POSTs from one network a valid token still suppresses'.

findings.title: REJECTED_DEFINITIVE{status} is an open port result: the application does not limit it to the definitive set, so an adapter that maps 500 there yields NOT_SENT
findings.reproduction: The port enum (cells:100) is REJECTED_DEFINITIVE{status} | HTTP_5XX{status} ...; A3 (plan:20) names 400, 403, 413 and 429 as definitive. The real Gmail adapter is a live half (PART B15/B19), and nothing in B12 refuses REJECTED_DEFINITIVE{500}.
findings.acceptance_criterion: The dispatcher treats any REJECTED_DEFINITIVE whose status is outside the closed set as SEND_UNCERTAIN, with a unit cell.
findings.failing_test: b12-dispatch-cells :: 'R2-129 (port misclassification): REJECTED_DEFINITIVE{500} from the port is SEND_UNCERTAIN, zero further submissions'.
